verdict.rationale: A package manager could plausibly ship its own background automations, such as scheduled auto-updates, so the axis applies. The evidence only shows that brew can be called non-interactively from administrative scripts and scheduled jobs. The scheduling itself would come from the host platform (cron/launchd/MDM) or user-side scripts, which earn no credit. Homebrew's own formula-bumping automation is maintainer infrastructure, not something a user sets up.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
